chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hajjal, from Dawood ibn Abi Yazid, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
And in another report: That is because his good deed ascends to Allah, so it is not spread among the people, whereas the disbeliever is appreciated.

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, to Whom deeds ultimately return
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer; the one characterized by iman
key_terms.مَعْرُوفَهُ: his good deed or recognized act of goodness
key_terms.مُكَفَّرٌ: unappreciated or not acknowledged among people
key_terms.يَصْعَدُ: ascends; rises up in acceptance to Allah
key_terms.يُنْشَرُ: is spread or publicized among people

ai.seo_question: Why is a believer sometimes not appreciated by people for his good deeds?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the believer may not receive recognition among people for his good deeds. Its significance is that the true worth and acceptance of righteous action is with Allah, while worldly praise is not the measure of a person's standing before Him.
